correctness.rationale: For each rank configuration, the right-shift operator is coordinatewise nilpotent: k successive active edges force a rank drop of k, so the XOR inverse terminates in at most the starting rank. The fixed-control map is a compact binary-group automorphism and preserves conditional Haar data, giving independent fair output bits. Given any window [-R,R], the truncated parity is correct if the rank chain stops; otherwise at least one unseen fair bit makes the true parity conditionally unbiased. Its Bayes error is exactly half the continuation probability, and no local decoder can improve it. Disjoint descending-rank cylinders give the arbitrary-rank distribution formula. The geometric series evaluates exactly, with quadratic logarithmic decay. Explicit opposite inverse outputs with the same finite window show nonreversibility. Exhaustive exact forward/inverse, finite-tail and Bayes-posterior checks are recorded in CHECK_OUTPUT.txt; finite checks are not treated as proof of the general statements.

value.rationale: A central obstruction in infinite-alphabet dynamics is loss of a uniform inverse memory even for a bijective nearest-neighbor cellular automaton. For a natural full-support geometric distribution on the source rank track, the exact optimal reconstruction error is not merely small: its logarithm has a sharp negative quadratic-in-radius law. The theorem identifies the measurable-vs-uniform locality boundary and supplies an optimal finite-window decoder with a matching Bayes lower bound, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, a simple restatement of bijectivity or a finite-only computation. It gives a reproducible quantitative benchmark for noncompact symbolic inversion and for model-specific finitary coding.
